module purpose: The neorv32_bus file groups several bus helper entities: a two-port arbiter/switch, an optional request/response register stage, an address gateway and 32-device I/O switch, and two blocks that sequence special read-then-write and conditional-write bus operations. Together they route bus_req_t/bus_rsp_t traffic, monitor timeouts, and modify request or response behavior using stored internal state.

use-case flows.value: arbitrate between request ports A and B, forward one shared request to X, and return the selected response status to the owning requester
retain the selected requester while its lock bit remains asserted
decode a request address to downstream ports, qualify request strobes, and merge enabled responses
raise a synthetic timeout acknowledgement/error when an outstanding gateway transfer expires without a halted fallback path
optionally register host requests and responses before forwarding them between bus stages
capture a special read-then-write request, wait for the read response, compute a replacement write value, issue the write, and return the preserved read data
track conditional-write reservation state, suppress or pass the system strobe for that request class, and report failure when the reservation state is absent
clear arbitration, monitor, read-modify-write, and conditional-write state when rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Shared-bus arbitration state, pending-request state, and issue decision
conceptual assets.reasoning: The switch stores current ownership and pending requests in `state`, `a_req`, `b_req`, and `sel_q` at lines 55-67, computes the next owner and request issue in lines 83-132, uses `sel` to choose which request fields drive `x_req_o` at lines 140-156, and gates returned `ack`/`err` to only one side at lines 164-169. Integrity is established because corrupting this state or decision misroutes the forwarded request or misattributes the returned status; availability is also established because `a_req` and `b_req` preserve pending strobes with `a_req <= a_req or a_req_i.stb` and `b_req <= b_req or b_req_i.stb` at lines 61 and 66.

The switch captures incoming lock bits with `locked_nxt <= b_req_i.lock & a_req_i.lock;` at line 111 and stores them in `locked` at line 57. In the busy states, lines 88-91 and 100-103 use `locked` to keep `stb` driven from the currently selected requester and to hold the FSM out of `S_IDLE` until the corresponding `.lock` deasserts, while non-locked transfers return to idle on `x_rsp_i.ack` at lines 93-106. Integrity is established because this stored lock state directly controls whether ownership is retained or released.

conceptual assets.concept: Address-based destination-port selection in the gateway logic
conceptual assets.reasoning: `port_sel` is computed from the request address and enabled-port base comparisons at lines 356-361, then line 378 uses it to qualify one `port_req(i).stb`, lines 366-369 drive the corresponding downstream request outputs, and lines 390-395/399-401 merge enabled responses. Integrity is established because correct routing requires the selected downstream port to match the implemented address decode. The same kind of address-qualified routing appears in `neorv32_bus_io_switch` at lines 660-665 and 685-690, but there the decision only survives on transport signals, so `port_sel` is the eligible structural reference.

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway outstanding-transfer monitor and timeout-error flag
conceptual assets.reasoning: The gateway stores whether a transfer is active, its lock status, a running counter, and whether the fallback X port was selected with `keeper.busy`, `keeper.lock`, `keeper.cnt`, and `keeper.halt` at lines 416-422. When the counter MSB becomes `1` while `keeper.halt = '0'`, line 424 sets `keeper.err`, line 425 clears `keeper.busy`, and lines 400-401 inject `keeper.err` into the reported `ack` and `err`. Integrity is established because timeout reporting and release conditions depend on these stored values; availability is also established because the monitor preserves progress state across cycles until `int_rsp.ack` or unlock at line 426-427.

The read-modify-write block captures and preserves its working context in the internal record `arbiter`: line 763 stores `arbiter <= arbiter_nxt`, while lines 777-785 load the next command, write operand, and read response and lines 780-801 advance through read-wait, execute, write, and write-wait states. Lines 813-828 then gate system request fields and returned response fields from this stored state. Integrity is established because the whole read/compute/write sequence depends on the correctness of this retained context; availability is established because the context is held across cycles until the sequence reaches `S_IDLE` again.

The replacement write value is computed in `alu_res` by the clocked case at lines 838-845 from the stored command and operands, with the compare path built at lines 850-853 and selected through `cmp_res`; line 813 uses `alu_res` as `sys_req_o.data` during the write states. Integrity is established because a wrong computed value changes the data written back by the read-then-write operation; availability is also established because `alu_res` is registered on `clk_i` for use by the write stage.

conceptual assets.concept: Conditional-write reservation state and failure result
conceptual assets.reasoning: This block stores a two-bit reservation/control state: lines 926-927 set `state` to `"10"` for the reservation-class read request, lines 910-915 decide whether a following write advances to `"11"` or clears back to `"00"`, and line 944 gates `sys_req_o.stb` with `state(1)` for the conditional write. Line 957 sets `sc_fail` when that write class arrives while `state(1)` is `0`, and lines 963-964 report the failure by forcing `ack` and OR-ing the failure bit into the response data. Integrity is established because both the permission to issue the conditional write and the reported success/failure result depend on this stored state and failure flag.
